system_description.narrative_title: Iran–US war driving maritime disruption and oil-market volatility
system_description.narrative_summary: An active U.S.–Iran military confrontation is producing acute disruption at maritime chokepoints (Strait of Hormuz, Red Sea), forcing shipping reroutes and shifting oil flows while sparking rapid oil-price swings. Tehran is publicly offering short ceasefires and proposals to reopen Hormuz even as U.S. leaders reportedly reject deals and U.S. institutions decline constraints on executive war powers. The interplay of battlefield events, diplomatic bargaining, commercial logistics, and market expectations creates tight feedbacks that amplify supply risk and geopolitical tension.
system_description.scope: Inside: the Iran–U.S. military confrontation and related regional proxy strikes (e.g., Houthi attacks); maritime chokepoints (Strait of Hormuz, Gulf of Oman, Red Sea); shipping and logistics responses (rerouting by DP World, ship-to-ship transfers); oil production, export flows (Saudi exports, pipelines), and price formation; diplomatic negotiations and U.S. domestic political decisions on war powers.
system_description.super_system: Global security and energy system (international geopolitics, global oil markets and supply chains)
adjacent_subsystems: Global oil markets and financial derivatives
Maritime shipping, insurance and logistics networks
U.S. domestic politics and war-powers institutions
Regional security architecture of the Gulf and Red Sea states

Trump rejects Iranian proposal to open Hormuz and end fighting

DP World Reroutes Cargo as Costs Mount From Hormuz Disruption
Oil Prices Jump on Houthi Attacks, U.S.-Iran Escalation Fears
Oil Prices Fall as U.S.-Iran Diplomacy and Regional Tensions Remain in Focus

variables.name: Military engagement intensity
variables.description: The overall level of kinetic and paramilitary actions between belligerents and proxies in the theater per unit time.

variables.name: Maritime chokepoint congestion
variables.description: The density of commercial and military transits and the effective capacity constraint at strategic straits and sea lanes.

variables.name: Shipping reroute rate
variables.description: The flow rate of commercial voyages being diverted from primary routes to alternative longer or safer corridors.

variables.name: Crude oil export flow volume
variables.description: The volumetric rate of crude oil exports moving through the maritime and pipeline network toward global markets.

variables.name: Crude oil price volatility
variables.description: The short- to medium-term variation and uncertainty in benchmark crude oil prices as reflected in spot and derivatives markets.

variables.name: Physical oil supply disruption
variables.description: The extent to which extraction, pipeline, storage, or export infrastructure is physically unavailable or impaired.

variables.name: Global oil inventory levels
variables.description: The stock of crude and refined product held in commercial and strategic storage available to cushion supply shocks.

variables.name: Naval military presence density
variables.description: The concentration of naval and maritime security assets operating in a given sea area.

variables.name: Maritime attack frequency
variables.description: The rate of hostile incidents against commercial shipping (attacks, interceptions, missile/projectile strikes) per time period.

variables.name: Insurance premia levels
variables.description: The prevailing cost-of-risk surcharges and war/route insurance premiums applied to maritime shipping and cargo.

variables.name: Diplomatic bargaining intensity
variables.description: The frequency and intensity of formal and informal negotiation interactions aimed at de-escalation or settlement.

variables.name: Domestic constraints on executive force
variables.description: The degree to which domestic legal, political, and institutional limits restrict executive authority to use military force.

variables.name: Shipping costs and freight rates
variables.description: The prevailing level of freight rates, fuel surcharges, and logistics costs for maritime cargo movement.

variables.name: Refining and logistics utilization
variables.description: The degree to which refining, storage, and inland logistics capacity are utilized to process and move crude and products.

variables.name: Market expectation of supply risk
variables.description: The market-implied assessment of future supply shortage probability and severity reflected in prices and sentiment.

variables.name: Pipeline flow utilization
variables.description: The rate and share of pipeline capacity currently in use for oil and product transfers between production and export points.

catalysts.title: Iran's 7-day Hormuz/ceasefire deadline
catalysts.description: Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and a 7-day ceasefire window could lead to rapid changes in transit access and tensions.
catalysts.rationale: Iran offers to reopen Strait of Hormuz within 7 days; Iran offers US new ‘7-day’ ceasefire proposal.

catalysts.title: Ongoing US–Iran phased-deal talks
catalysts.description: Continued negotiations on a phased deal to reopen Hormuz and end the blockade that could progressively de-escalate the maritime disruption.
catalysts.rationale: US and Iran discuss phased deal to reopen Hormuz and end US blockade; Iran offers to restart talks.

catalysts.title: French deployment to protect Saudi Red Sea port
catalysts.description: France's announced deployment to protect a Saudi Red Sea oil port increases regional military presence and alters security dynamics around shipping lanes.
catalysts.rationale: France to deploy forces to protect Saudi Red Sea oil port; France to send military to protect Saudi Arabia on Red Sea oil route.

catalysts.title: DP World cargo rerouting
catalysts.description: Major port operator DP World is shifting cargo routes in response to war disruptions, triggering sustained rerouting and cost increases across maritime logistics.
catalysts.rationale: DP World Shifts Routes as Costs From War Disruptions Rise; DP World Reroutes Cargo as Costs Mount From Hormuz Disruption.

catalysts.title: Ship‑to‑ship transfers in Gulf of Oman reach capacity
catalysts.description: STS transfer capacity in the Gulf of Oman has reached limits amid a Saudi export surge, constraining immediate export throughput and routing options.
catalysts.rationale: Gulf of Oman ship-to-ship oil transfers reach limit as Saudi exports surge; Crude exports via Hormuz at 33.7 million barrels this week.

catalysts.title: US rejection of ceasefire — escalation risk
catalysts.description: U.S. rejection of Iran's ceasefire proposal raises the risk of renewed US strikes (reportedly 'after midterms'), increasing military and market volatility risks.
catalysts.rationale: Trump rejects Iran ceasefire; Exclusive: Trump Expects Renewed Bombing After Midterms; Senate rejects resolution curbing war powers.

catalysts.title: Potential resumption of Saudi East‑West pipeline loading
catalysts.description: Sources indicate pipeline volumes are building; resumption of loading would raise exports and pipeline utilization, easing maritime transfer pressure.
catalysts.rationale: Saudi East-West Pipeline building up volumes, loading yet to resume; Saudi crude exports hit highest level since Iran war began.

catalysts.title: Options-market contrarian signal on oil prices
catalysts.description: Derivatives positions are signaling a contrarian view on oil; this may alter short-term volatility and market risk expectations unpredictably.
catalysts.rationale: The options market is sending a contrarian signal about oil prices; markets react to U.S.-Iran diplomacy and attacks.
